raw_response:
Two candidates survived catalogue discovery and primary verification. Neither was established as available by the 2010-03-21 decision cutoff.

1. Repology version-comparison mechanism — https://repology.org/

Repology's documented component-and-rank comparator could supply an implementable order for heterogeneous numeric, prerelease, postrelease and letter-suffix versions, with bound sentinels for testing release-prefix intervals. Its primary algorithm description splits numeric and alphabetic components, ranks recognized release markers, compares numeric values, and pads missing components; the upper/lower-bound extension supports prefix-range membership. This could help compare existing upstream and distribution spellings without relying on upload order. Transfer caveat: its heuristic handling of ambiguous suffixes and first-letter alphabetic comparison can collapse distinct spellings, and version order does not establish API compatibility. The exact algorithm's date is unknown; the opened discovery listing was added in 2019 and updated in 2024, so no pre-cutoff availability is claimed.

Discovery catalogue: https://alternativeto.net/software/repology/about/
Primary verification: https://github.com/repology/repology-updater and https://github.com/repology/libversion/blob/master/doc/ALGORITHM.md

2. Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence rules — https://semver.org/

Semantic Versioning supplies deterministic numeric and prerelease precedence rules that can make declared compatibility intervals independent of upload order when package producers adopt its API-change contract. It defines an ordered numeric core, prerelease ordering, and the exclusion of build metadata from precedence, alongside a bounded dependency-interval example. Transfer caveat: its fixed grammar does not directly accommodate every existing date-based, custom or distribution-revision version, so explicit migration or mapping rules remain necessary, and producer compatibility declarations still need validation. The opened 2.0.0 specification has no publication date. The original author's 2022-05-23 discussion is later evidence and does not establish exact version publication or availability by the cutoff.

Discovery catalogue: https://alternativeto.net/software/semantic-release/about/
Verification route: the catalogue's official documentation link at https://semantic-release.gitbook.io/semantic-release explicitly links https://semver.org/.
Dated supplementary primary evidence: https://tom.preston-werner.com/2022/05/23/major-version-numbers-are-not-sacred

I did not retain APT because its official wiki was blocked and its accessible source landing page did not establish the required ordering mechanics. Release-automation-only catalogue entries were also omitted. This is an internal-model translation of documented mechanisms, not evidence that either candidate was deployed or proved useful for the design problem.
